rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> factorial randomized block field experiment at Wadi El-Tor, South Sinai, winter 2021, three replicates, two N rates x four drip fertigation schedules plus regular-irrigation control. Q2: Results, 'Potato Yield and Yield Components' and Table 4 <U+2013> drip fertigation schedules increased tuber yield by 25.32% (N1, 240 kg N/ha) and 36.47% (N2, 360 kg N/ha) over regular irrigation with soil-applied N; this matches the passage figures. Q4: Table 5 and Fig. 2 <U+2013> total N uptake, N recovery and NUE measured per treatment, yield highly correlated with N uptake (R2 0.98/0.96); Fig. 3 <U+2013> soil NO3-N at 0<U+2013>20 and 20<U+2013>40 cm showing fertigation keeps nitrate in the root zone while regular irrigation moves it to deeper layers; Table 4 <U+2013> LAI higher under fertigation. These are measured intermediates linking drip fertigation to yield.
rows.notes: Single site, single sandy soil, one crop and one season; yield measured by one method (plot harvest), so no triangulation, representativeness or scaling. Q7 doubtful: conclusion states that leaching is possible in sandy soil even with drip and that applied nutrients must not be subject to leaching, and that benefits were greater with stage-wise weekly scheduling, but these read as recommendations/variation rather than stated requirements for the drip-vs-regular yield effect. Q8: no explicit limitations given beyond noting the result applies to sandy soil texture. Q9: Table 3 reports CV% (2.61 for tuber yield) and Table 4 uses LSD letter groupings; no SD, SE, CI or range for the yield increase itself, so rated no. Note that the comparison confounds irrigation method (drip vs regular) with fertilizer application method (fertigation vs soil-applied), so the effect is of drip fertigation as a package.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a one-season field trial on sandy soil in Egypt comparing drip fertigation schedules with regular irrigation plus soil-applied N; the passage reproduces the study's own reported yield increases (25.32% and 36.47%).
